findings.title: Adding non-default getShortcut breaks existing grant provider implementations
findings.body: `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` now has a new abstract `getShortcut()` method. Any custom grant factory compiled against an older Keycloak does not implement it. `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` calls `getShortcut()` for every registered OAuth2 grant factory during server startup, so such an extension will throw `AbstractMethodError` and prevent startup. Make this a default method with a safe fallback, or explicitly tolerate providers that do not implement it.

findings.title: Decoder hard-codes 2-character shortcuts but the factory contract does not
findings.body: The decoder assumes the encoded prefix is exactly 6 characters and splits it into three fixed 2-character fields. The grant field comes from `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()`, whose contract does not enforce a 2-character value (its Javadoc even says 'usually like 3-letters'). A custom grant returning e.g. `foo` will be encoded successfully as `onrtfoo:<id>`, but `getTokenContextFromTokenId` will then reject it because the prefix is 7 characters. Enforce the length at registration or make the decoder length-aware; otherwise Keycloak can issue tokens that it cannot parse itself.

findings.title: validateToken unconditionally tags recreated tokens as refresh-token grant
findings.body: `validateToken` recreates an access token from an existing `oldToken`, and this new line always stores `refresh_token` in `Constants.GRANT_TYPE`. This method is used outside the refresh flow as well (legacy token exchange uses it while validating the subject token and producing the exchanged access token), so those exchanged tokens get the refresh shortcut `rt` instead of the actual token-exchange grant. The grant type should be set by the calling flow, as `StandardTokenExchangeProvider` does, or only set to refresh in the refresh-specific path.

findings.title: Constructor checks grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
findings.body: The second `Objects.requireNonNull` call is intended to validate `rawTokenId`, but it still passes `grantType` with the message `Null rawTokenId not allowed`. A null raw token ID is therefore accepted. In `encodeTokenId`, concatenating a null raw ID produces the literal string `onrtac:null`, so multiple tokens can share the same `jti` rather than failing fast. Change the second check to `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId has an inverted/wrong grant-shortcut check
findings.body: For an ID like `onrtac:<uuid>`, the grant shortcut occupies indices 4-6 (`ac`), but the matcher reads `substring(3, 5)` (`ta`) and returns false when that value equals the expected shortcut. As written, the grant portion is effectively never checked: any correctly shaped prefix with a UUID suffix passes. If the substring were corrected without also fixing the condition, correct IDs would be rejected. Use `items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)` for the positive check and guard the prefix length to avoid `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException`.

findings.title: Incorrect-grant test passes on NPE instead of testing the intended failure
findings.body: The test's `before` method constructs the factory but never sets a `KeycloakSessionFactory`. Looking up an unknown shortcut such as `ac` therefore calls `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)` on null and throws NPE. The test catches any `RuntimeException`, so it passes without ever verifying the intended `IllegalArgumentException` for an unknown grant shortcut. Initialize the factory dependency and assert the exception type/message.
